title: Agro puppet
brief_description:
Agro was loud, messy and rude in the way that Australians loved. Performed by Jamie Dunn, the mischievous hand puppet became one of Australian children’s television’s most recognisable characters. He appeared on Boris’ Breakfast Club (1981–89), Wombat (1982–90), The Super Saturday Show (1989) and later fronted Agro’s Cartoon Connection (1990–97).

Agro’s appeal came from the gap between puppet and person. He behaved like a cheeky human host, but his ping-pong ball eyes, gravelly voice and shaggy fur made him clearly not human. Dunn usually stayed hidden behind furniture, while Agro joked with presenters, teased guests and often referred to being a puppet, including his unmoving limbs and the hand up his back. That gave Agro his ability to misbehave – the more obviously a puppet he was, the further the joke could go.

Since Dunn’s passing in 2026, Agro also carries the memory of a performer whose voice, timing and mischief made him so beloved.
